title: Longest Happy Prefix
summary: Identify the longest segment at the start of a string that also matches its ending, excluding the segment itself.
statement: Identify the longest segment at the start of a string that also matches its ending, excluding the segment itself. Return an empty string if no such segment exists.
constraints: A happy prefix is non-empty, proper, and also a suffix.
Return the longest one, or the empty string when none exists.
reference_solution:
def longest_happy_prefix(s):
 failure=[0]*len(s)
 for i in range(1,len(s)):
  length=failure[i-1]
  while length and s[i]!=s[length]:length=failure[length-1]
  if s[i]==s[length]:length+=1
  failure[i]=length
 return s[:failure[-1]]
hints: Build the KMP failure array over the entire string.
On mismatch, follow failure links to the next possible border.
The final failure value is the longest proper prefix also ending at the final character.
Failure links test every viable border in linear time.
